meta_title: Children’s game — The Lord of the Rings 2026
description: Programme for children roughly aged 5 to 10 during The Lord of the Rings 2026: games, crafts, forest activities, courage path and Saturday adventure across stations.
title: Children’s game
subtitle: Young adventurers have their own quests in Middle-earth.
h_who: Who is the children’s game for?
who_p1: The children’s game is for children who are still too young for the main battle but want to enjoy their own adventure, games, crafts, stations and the atmosphere of Middle-earth.
who_p2_pre: The main battle and event participation is from
who_p2_post: . For younger participants we run a separate children’s game.
age_card1_p: The main target group of the children’s game. By arrangement, children around 10 can also join if the programme suits them.
age_card2_p: Only with a parent or another responsible adult. Without a parent or close adult it isn’t possible.
age_note: We are not a kindergarten or babysitting service — we want to give children an adventure, but safety and well-being always come first.
h_60s: The most important things in 60 seconds
s60_l1: The main game and battle is age 12+.
s60_l2: For younger children we run a separate children’s game.
s60_l3_pre: The children’s game is mainly for children
s60_l4: Younger children aged 3–5 can only join with a parent.
s60_l5: The programme runs mainly on Friday and on Saturday during the main game.
s60_l6: On Saturday we run stations, tasks and the kids’ own adventure.
s60_l7: We ask parents for cooperation, help and a realistic assessment of their child’s abilities.
s60_l8: Parental involvement is welcome and very much appreciated.
h_program: When does the children’s game take place?
program_note: The times are indicative — we’ll refine them based on preparation and weather. Children’s safety and well-being take precedence over an exact schedule.
p1_title: Children’s team game on the meadow
p1_desc: If you arrive with children already on Thursday, we plan from about 16:00 onwards a lighter introductory programme — a team game, movement activities or a more relaxed programme depending on the situation.
p2_desc: Sports games, low rope obstacles, drawing and crafts, archery-style shooting, throwing at targets, forest activities, a jewellery-making workshop and other small games and stations.
p3_desc: A short atmospheric path of courage ending with a scene with elves. We adjust it to the age and courage of the children.
p4_desc: Tasks, physical activities, riddles, puzzles, throwing, treasure hunting and small story elements. Includes a snack or “lunch from the hobbit pantry”.
p5_desc: After returning to the meadow, a more relaxed programme, crafts or further activities until the armies return from the main game.
program_alert_pre: The programme may change based on the weather, the number of children, ages and conditions on site.
program_alert_strong: Children’s safety and well-being take precedence over an exact schedule.
what_p1: The children’s game is meant to be playful, safe and atmospheric. It isn’t a small copy of the main battle. Children don’t need to fight like adult players. We want to offer them their own adventure where they can be small hobbits, elves, dwarves, messengers, treasure hunters or brave wanderers.
parents_p1: Parents are important for the children’s game. We will be glad if you:
parents_l1: help the children prepare a simple costume,
parents_l2: explain to them what awaits them,
parents_l3: remain available if we need you,
parents_l5: join in the programme if it appeals to you.
parents_p2: For younger children, parental participation is necessary. For older children it depends on their independence, courage and an arrangement on site.
parents_p3: We very much appreciate parental involvement. The more good adult hands we have, the nicer and safer an adventure we can build for the children.

take_l1: comfortable clothes for forest and meadow,
safety_intro: We adapt the children’s programme to the age and abilities of the children. Even so:
safety_l1: the parent is responsible for their child,
safety_l3: children must follow the instructions of the programme leaders,
safety_l4: in case of tiredness, fear or discomfort, it’s OK to stop an activity,
safety_l5: the child should know where to find the parents,
safety_l6: parents should be available during the programme.
safety_alert_strong: a medical limitation, allergy, significant fear, special needs
safety_alert_post: or anything we should know about, write to us in advance and remind us on site.

cta_body: Let us know in the registration. We’ll prepare the children their own slice of Middle-earth — with tasks, crafts, courage, laughter and a treasure that won’t be guarded by just any old dragon.
cta_footnote: The detailed programme and contact person for the children’s game will be published together with concrete times and the team running it.
